newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off lows, seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off lows, seen rebounding.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended easier, but above their lows, in sleepy trade on Wednesday as players failed to find much inspiration in the Dow's surge to a new record close overnight.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract recovered from a low of 20,010 to end at 20,125, 50 points below its previous close.
Dealers said the market had remained well supported at the psychological 20,000 level.
"I think we should rebound from here tomorrow. But there would be profit-taking near 20,500-20,600," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.
"I don't think the Nikkei is going to break above 21,000 in the near term. The fundamentals still don't look so good for the Japanese market," he added.
He said the dollar's weaker tone against the yen and the fact that foreigners remained net sellers of Tokyo stocks on Wednesday despite Wall Street's rally had weighed on the market.
Taiwan stock index futures finished lower in line with heavy profit-taking in Taipei shares.
The July MSCI Taiwan index contract lost 7.4 points to end at 402.3 on volume of 2,130 lots.
